messages:
Evan: Heads-up — customer ticket #C-9281. They invoked the refund flow but our router routed to create_charge (legacy) and charged the card. Customer angry. Repro steps + payload below. Can someone triage?

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-45. Assigned to @Maya and @Josh. :rotating_light:

Evan: Summary: customer calls /v1/actions with tool hint "refund" via our SDK. The auto-router chose `legacy_charge.create` instead of `payments.issue_refund`. No schema validation error — call succeeded and a charge was created.

Evan: Repro payload we received from the SDK (redacted):
```json
{
  "session_id": "sess_abc123",
  "user_id": "acct_789",
  "tool_hint": "refund",
  "args": {
    "transaction_id": "tx_555",
    "amount": 49.99,
    "currency": "USD",
    "reason": "customer_requested"
  }
}
```

Evan: Router log excerpt (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] route_decision: input_hint="refund" candidate_tools=["payments.issue_refund","legacy_charge.create","credit.apply_credit"] scores=[0.48,0.50,0.02] selected="legacy_charge.create" policy="auto" note="tie-breaker: name_similarity"
```

Maya: :eyes: That score vector looks like a tie where name similarity tipped it. The model/heuristic is over-weighting `create` because legacy tool has alias `refund_charge` in metadata. Any chance the SDK sent an alias token?

Evan: Not that we can see — SDK sends just the tool_hint string. Customer says they typed "refund" in chat. No alias token.

Josh: Quick check: can you paste the full tool metadata for legacy_charge and payments? Might be an overlap in descriptions. Also do we have the original request_id so I can pull request logs and KV cache?

Evan: request_id: rreq_20260312_9x. Tool metadata snapshot attached by support-bot below.

support-bot: tool-meta (snapshot): legacy_charge.aliases=["charge","refund_charge","create_charge"], description="Legacy payment capture and adjustments"; payments.issue_refund.aliases=["refund","issue_refund"], description="Issue a refund to a transaction id"

Maya: There it is — legacy tool still has alias `refund_charge`. The selector's fuzzy-match treats `refund` ~ `refund_charge` as high similarity. We should tighten alias matching or prefer exact alias matches to avoid these swaps.

Laura: Customer wants a fast mitigation: can we add a routing override on their account to pin to payments.*? They are on Dedicated so we can add a policy.

Josh: Yes, add per-customer routing policy. Quick example to push to routing config (applies immediately):
```yaml
customers:
  acct_789:
    prefer_tools: ["payments.issue_refund"]
    fallback: ["payments.issue_refund"]
```

Josh: Long term: adjust selector weights — lower alias fuzzy match weight and add a whitelist for verb-exact matches. I'll open a PR with tests.

Maya: Also: add a schema-level safety check: if tool_hint exact equals "refund" and args contains "transaction_id", force prefer payments.issue_refund. Minimal heuristic to stop customer-impacting swaps.

Evan: For troubleshooting: customer log shows the SDK call's Content-Type and body matched, no retries. They got a 200 with charge id `ch_999`. We need a reversal path and customer apology kit.

Laura: I initiated a manual reversal and refund for ch_999. Pending confirmation from payments. Also offered expedited refund and a $25 credit. Customer accepted.

Maya: I'll own the selector fix and a postmortem doc. Plan: (1) emergency alias cleanup — remove `refund_charge` from legacy aliases, (2) add exact-match precedence, (3) add unit tests for ambiguous hints, (4) deploy canary to staging and Dedicated.

Josh: Filed ENG ticket ENG-4021. ETA for canary: 48h. Will monitor related routes for similar patterns.

Evan: Thanks. Please add notes to the ticket about fallback behavior and backfill logs for all `refund` hints in the last 7 days so CS can contact any other affected customers.

support-bot: ENG-4021 created, severity=P2, linked INC-2026-45. :white_check_mark:

Josh: Quick repro command for devs if you want to try locally:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/actions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tool_hint":"refund","args":{"transaction_id":"tx_555","amount":49.99}}'
```
Maya: I'll post a short postmortem once the fix is merged. For now removing risky aliases is blocking action. :lock:
